analysis: The PR adds a coordinator-triggered update check on the runtime_status{verified:false} event. Serve.swift:376 calls handleRuntimeOutdatedEvent, which records the mismatch and calls triggerRuntimeOutdatedUpdateCheckIfDue (AutoUpdate.swift:204-222). That function fires a tracked Task running the existing performAutoUpdateCheck. The trigger honors auto_update, DARKBLOOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK, a 10-minute spacing (RuntimeOutdatedUpdateTrigger, not supplied) and a single-flight guard on the tracked task. The coordinator is trusted, so this adds no new adversarial input path. A malicious coordinator or MITM could already drive updates through the periodic poll. Update authenticity is unchanged: SelfUpdater download/verify/stage, the cross-process lease in claimUpdateStart, and the drain-then-commit sequence with ownsUpdateDrain and App Attest worker stop fences in commitInstall and restartAfterAutoUpdate. The event path cannot bypass these because it reuses performAutoUpdateCheck. Teardown handling is consistent. Lifecycle.swift:62-64 and Serve.swift:459-460 cancel and clear runtimeOutdatedUpdateTask, and the ID-token check at AutoUpdate.swift:229-233 avoids clobbering. A cancelled task relies on the controller's cancellation fences (commitStagedUpdateBundle checks Task.isCancelled and drain ownership) to withhold the commit and restart. Unverified items: the RuntimeOutdatedUpdateTrigger implementation, SelfUpdater signature and qualification checks, and the declaration of runtimeOutdatedUpdateTask, runtimeOutdatedUpdateTaskID, lastRuntimeUpdateCheckAt and recordRuntimeOutdated. Their definitions are outside the supplied units. A residual availability consideration is that a compromised coordinator can force update cycles and drains, bounded by the 10-minute spacing. Relevant IDs: TB-002, T-013, T-043. No concrete regression is established.
